data.name: Antigua and Barbuda
data.summary: Antigua and Barbuda does not tax individuals' income (personal income tax was abolished in 2016), and has no capital gains, dividend, inheritance, estate or wealth tax. Self-employment and unincorporated business income bears unincorporated business tax (0-25%). Real estate transfers are costly: 7.5% seller and 2.5% buyer stamp duty, a 5% alien landholding licence for non-resident buyers and 5% tax on appreciation for non-resident sellers. Citizenship by investment from USD 230,000 (National Development Fund) or USD 300,000 real estate.

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: No personal income tax; unincorporated business tax on self-employment/business income only.
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident; non-citizens need a residence permit or citizenship.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax on securities or business interests. Land sales by non-residents/non-citizens bear a 5% tax on the appreciation.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on sale of real property: 7.5% seller and 2.5% purchaser on value. Non-resident purchasers also need an Alien Landholding Licence costing 5% of value; non-resident sellers pay 5% stamp tax on the appreciation in value (the IRD lists a 'Non-Citizen Land Appreciation Tax' paid at the time of sale). Share sales: 5% seller, 2.5% buyer. Undeveloped land owned by non-residents: annual 10-20% tax on land value.

income.name: Antigua and Barbuda

income_tax.summary: No personal income tax on employment income. A resident self-employed person pays the unincorporated business tax (UBT) on worldwide net business income: 0% up to XCD 42,000, 8% to XCD 186,000 and 25% above; this is modelled as the brackets (employees do not pay it). Employees pay 7% social security plus 3.5% medical benefits up to XCD 6,500 a month; the self-employed pay 10% social security on declared earnings.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Social security for the self-employed is 10% of declared insurable earnings (Social Security (Self Employed Persons) Regulations 2013, reg. 9(1), S.I. 17 of 2013); professionals, consultants and IT specialists fall in class V and must declare at least XCD 6,000 a month (Schedule substituted by S.I. 59 of 2016). The XCD 78,000 cap is the employee ceiling of XCD 6,500 a month (Deloitte); the Regulations do not state a separate self-employed ceiling. Third-party guides add 5% for the medical benefits scheme; that was not confirmed on an official page and is not included. UBT is due quarterly on net income after expenses (IRD FAQ; Deloitte 2026); the registration fee (XCD 0 to 400 by gross income) counts against the tax. Self-employed people pay the unincorporated business tax; whether their own social security contributions are deductible from it was not established. The employee figure (0, no tax) governs.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Antigua and Barbuda has had no personal income tax since 2016 (IRD FAQ), but resident individuals pay the unincorporated business tax on worldwide self-employment income (Deloitte 2026; IRD FAQ bands for a sole trader: 0% to XCD 42,000, 8% to XCD 186,000, 25% above). The self-employed brackets are those UBT bands, because a resident freelancer with foreign clients is taxed on that income and no exemption for Nomad Digital Residence holders could be found (see the regime). Employees pay no income tax, so the wage brackets are nil. Employee contributions: social security 7% and medical benefits 3.5% (Deloitte), ceiling XCD 6,500 a month. A 17% sales tax applies, with registration compulsory for professional service providers.

regimes.name: Nomad Digital Residence (NDR)
regimes.description: Special-resident authorisation for people whose work can be done remotely for an employer or business outside Antigua and Barbuda, valid for up to two years in the first instance. Local employment is not allowed. No official statement that holders are exempt from income tax or UBT could be found, so it is recorded as a visa with standard taxation.
regimes.duration_note: Up to two years in the first instance; renewal terms were not found. Fee USD 1,500 single, USD 2,000 couple, USD 3,000 family of three or more.

income.residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship can apply for the Nomad Digital Residence (USD 50,000 a year, two-year authorisation, USD 1,500 single). Employees of a local employer need a work permit (not researched). Citizenship by investment (National Development Fund USD 230,000 or approved real estate from USD 300,000, per the CIU pages cited in data/jurisdictions/ATG.json) is a separate route. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income and have no Antigua tax to credit on employment income.

succession.name: Antigua and Barbuda
succession.summary: Antigua and Barbuda follows English common law, with no forced heirship found. It has an International Trust Act (2007) and private foundation legislation. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for it.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Antigua's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
succession.trust_note: Antigua is not in the HCCH status table. The International Trust Act 2007 (Act 18 of 2007) has sections on claims based on relationship and non-recognition of foreign judgments; a commercial guide says foreign forced-heirship judgments are not recognised. IFC Review lists Antigua among Caribbean states with private foundation laws; the Act's name was not confirmed.
open_questions: No source read confirms the absence of forced heirship or family provision claims in Antigua.
The foundation statute's name and text were not read.
Text of the 2007 Act's firewall sections not read.

immigration.name: Antigua and Barbuda
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone. Citizenship by investment starts at USD 230,000 (National Development Fund) or USD 300,000 in approved real estate, plus about USD 18,800 in processing, due diligence and passport fees for a single applicant. The Nomad Digital Residence visa (USD 1,500, income USD 50,000 a year, up to 2 years) suits remote workers. US restrictions on Antiguan passport holders since 1 January 2026 reduce the passport's value for US-bound travel.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation residence period not verified in this research; see open questions.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is generally allowed for CBI citizens (not verified against the Citizenship Act this pass).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: National Development Fund (NDF)
routes.summary: A USD 230,000 non-refundable contribution to the National Development Fund, the same for any family size, gives citizenship.
routes.requirements: USD 230,000 one-time contribution per application. Single applicant fees: processing USD 10,000, due diligence USD 8,500, passport USD 300. Family of up to four: processing USD 20,000; USD 10,000 per extra dependant. Dependants: spouse due diligence USD 5,000; child 12-17 USD 2,000; 18-30 and parents 55+ USD 4,000. 10% government fee due and non-refundable at submission. Interview required. Banned or restricted nationalities not confirmed (see open questions). US Proclamation 10998 (effective 1 January 2026) reportedly suspends new tourist, student, exchange and immigrant visas for Antiguan citizens, citing the programme; commercial sources only.
routes.investment_options: NDF USD 230,000; real estate USD 300,000; UWI Fund USD 260,000 (page ambiguous on whether it includes processing fees); business USD 1,500,000 single or USD 5,000,000 joint (min 2 investors, USD 400,000 each).
routes.fees_note: Single applicant: processing 10,000 + due diligence 8,500 + passport 300. Excludes agent and legal fees.
routes.physical_presence: 5 days in Antigua and Barbuda within the first 5 years after citizenship. A bill presented 14 July 2026 would raise this to 30 days; per the Prime Minister it already applies administratively under the regional framework. Not enacted as of the source.
routes.processing_time: Not sourced from the CIU this pass.
routes.family: Extra dependants: child 0-5 USD 10,000; 6-17 USD 25,000; 18+ USD 50,000 (plus fees).
routes.tax_note: No personal income tax; citizenship alone does not change tax residence elsewhere.
